utterances.text: Well, what's coming up next week will be a little bit more terminology, measures, and then we'll continue with replacing some of your notes. We'll look at the BPM and the overall phrasing.
The what? BPM? What's a BPM? Is that a type of piano?
Oh! No, sorry. Beats Per Minute. It’s just how we talk about the tempo now. It's the same thing as the speed.
Oh, well, you young people have a fancy name for everything. Back in my day, we just called it the time. Anyway, B is 2.
Right. If you want to move ahead a little bit, you can actually.
I played Mary Had a Little Lamb.
You did? Really? Did you count? Did you say tick-tock?

No. Yeah, I tried. I tried. Okay. You want me to do it for you? Okay, let's do it. Mary had a little lamb. Mary had a little lamb, let's go. There's really nothing new here except for you've replaced D with number 2. Right. I forget the tick-tock. I'll say it.
Okay. Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, tick.
See? Oh, I thought you said—
Oh, that's right, there's this one. Okay. Tick-tock. Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock. Whoops!
Oh, I forgot that one.
The rest. Okay. Now we're starting over again. We're gonna start right here. Fourth measure. Yeah.
We use this?
No. 1, 2, 3, fourth measure. We didn't talk about that. These little boxes are called measures. So if I say fourth measure, that's where you start.
Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock... Tick-tock! D? Last line—
You're here now with me again.
No I'm used to it. B's turn. Number two yeah. Tickle-tackle-tiltle.
Yeah that was good. Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock. That is, tock, tick, tock.
Right.
You can practice all the way to 'Mary Had a Little Lamb.' To 'Mary Had a Little Lamb.' Yes. I'll do that. Okay. You did good.
You think I'm doing good? Yes. Really? Don't just tell me that. Do you like it, Grandma?
Your fingers are moving.

Well, I'm learning. I'm learning more. Sometimes I forget what D is, or you know, I'm doing pretty good at remembering, but once in a while I forget the letters, what letters will go where, which finger.
That's normal. That's it.
Yeah, that's normal. At first, yeah. At first it's normal. I'm glad. That makes me feel good.
Okay. So I think you're doing perfect. You're doing good, Grandma. I'm not just saying that. I'm— yeah, I really do care.
You really do. You're not just saying it because I'm your grandma.
No.
Because— yeah, don't say it like that. Make— Make me work as hard as anyone else.
I will.
Okay, I'll practice till you get back next week.
Okay, Grandma.
